name: Filled Pure Sample Jar
summary: In Ironforge, Laris Geardawdle studies how corruption changes living matter. A Filled Pure Sample Jar holds primordial ooze from the remote wilds, giving him a clean specimen for comparison.

sections.title: A Search for Uncorrupted Slime
sections.body: Laris Geardawdle studies oozes across Azeroth and how corruption changes living matter. He found that these shapeless creatures absorb the magic and conditions of their homes, then reflect them. After cataloging tainted slimes in Felwood, he sought a clean sample for comparison. A Filled Pure Sample Jar holds primordial ooze gathered from the wilds of Un'Goro Crater, away from corrupted strains.

sections.title: Primordial Ecology
sections.body: Oozes change readily, so Laris cannot find pure samples near civilization, demonic blights, or necromantic fallout. The glutinous oozes of Un'Goro Crater's untamed basin remain relatively isolated from outside corruption. That makes them a useful standard for scholars in Ironforge.

aliases: who needs filled pure sample jar
faq.answer: Laris Geardawdle, a gnomish researcher in Ironforge, seeks pure samples to study Azeroth's ooze populations.

faq.q: Why does Laris need pure ooze instead of tainted ooze?
faq.answer: Laris found that slimes quickly absorb properties of their surroundings, including Felwood's demonic rot. He needs uncorrupted samples to compare with tainted ooze and understand how far corruption reaches and how it works.

faq.q: Where can pure ooze samples be collected?
aliases: where do i find pure ooze
faq.answer: Pure samples come from the glutinous oozes in Un'Goro Crater's primordial wilderness, where they remain isolated from outside blights.

faq.q: What happens once the samples are delivered to Ironforge?
aliases: what does laris do with them
faq.answer: Laris uses the samples to test how oozes adapt to and withstand their environment. He rewards adventurers who brave hazardous wilds to bring them to Ironforge.

angles.text: As a gnome, you can help scholars study living matter by comparing Felwood's tainted slimes with pure Un'Goro specimens.
As an Alliance explorer, you can bring knowledge of remote places like Un'Goro Crater to scholars in Ironforge.
